targets: difference between true synchronous mode and self controlled mode
html:
Difference Between True Synchronous Mode and Self Controlled Mode

The difference between true synchronous mode and self controlled mode lies in where the inverter takes its output frequency from when it drives a synchronous motor. In true synchronous mode the stator frequency is set independently by the drive oscillator and the rotor must follow it. In self controlled mode a rotor position sensor sets the stator frequency, so the stator field always stays in step with the rotor.

PointTrue synchronous modeSelf controlled mode
Frequency sourceIndependent oscillator in the driveRotor position or speed sensor feedback
Control typeOpen loop speed controlClosed loop, frequency follows rotor
Speed changeFrequency must be ramped slowlyFast changes possible without pull out
Hunting and loss of synchronismPossible on sudden load or frequency changeAvoided, rotor and field stay locked
Typical useSeveral motors run together at one frequencySingle motor drives needing fast response
BehaviourLike a normal synchronous motor on a variable supplySimilar to a DC motor with electronic commutation

In both modes speed still follows Ns = 120 × f / P. The difference is only whether f is commanded first and the rotor follows, or the rotor position commands f. Self controlled operation is the basis of brushless DC and commutatorless motor drives.
